facts: Signed Contoso updater launched msiexec during its scheduled 02:00 window.
It downloaded only from updates.contoso.example using a pinned certificate.
No persistence or credential access occurred.
BackupAgent ran vssadmin list shadows at 01:05, its documented backup window.
The parent is signed BackupAgent.exe and the host has the approved backup job.
No deletion command or outbound transfer occurred.
Signed AcmeInventoryAgent launched PowerShell Get-CimInstance during maintenance.
It wrote a local JSON inventory file.
No network connection, encoded command, persistence, or credential access occurred.
The approved network scanner authenticated to its assigned subnet at 03:00.
Its source IP, destination range, and change ticket match the scan schedule.
No hosts outside scope were contacted.
Word spawned PowerShell with -EncodedCommand for a user who opened an invoice attachment.
The payload decoded to a network request to an unapproved domain.
No child process or persistence was captured.
An unsigned process created a Run key and a scheduled task.
It connected every five minutes to a newly registered domain.
The domain returned encrypted command blobs.
A user-launched cleanup tool attempted to delete endpoint-agent logs.
The tool is unsigned and not in the approved software catalog.
No other persistence or network behavior is available.
A signed vulnerability scanner queried SMB version information.
The source is approved and the scan ticket covers the targets.
It used no exploit attempts or credential dumping behavior.
A VPN login occurred from a country not used by the employee in the last year.
MFA succeeded and the device is managed.
No impossible-travel corroboration or risky follow-on activity is available.
A service account created a new local administrator outside a change window.
The account then disabled audit logging.
The source workstation is not an administration jump host.
A developer executed git, npm, and docker commands in the approved build workspace.
The activity occurred during a recorded deployment.
No production credentials or external destinations were accessed.
A user granted a third-party OAuth application mailbox-read permission.
The application is not in the approved SaaS catalog.
There is no evidence of mailbox access yet.
A process rapidly encrypted user documents and deleted shadow copies.
It left a ransom note in each directory.
The process contacted a known ransomware payment site.
Windows Update initiated a reboot after approved monthly patching.
The update source was Microsoft and the maintenance window matches.
No unexpected processes ran before reboot.
An unsigned process opened LSASS with read permissions.
The process is not an approved security or backup product.
No memory dump file or credential use was observed.
A certificate-management service replaced an expiring TLS certificate.
The new certificate matches the approved CA and host name.
The operation follows its scheduled renewal window.
An unknown archive tool compressed finance data.
It uploaded the archive to an unapproved cloud-storage account.
The user has no business need for that destination.
A monitoring agent queried CPU, disk, and process health every five minutes.
The binary is signed and installed by the approved monitoring platform.
The telemetry went only to the documented monitoring endpoint.
A workstation made many DNS lookups for algorithmically generated names.
The endpoint agent did not identify a matching approved application.
No successful connection was recorded.
An administrator account disabled endpoint protection on three servers.
The action occurred outside the approved maintenance window.
The same account then opened remote shells from an unmanaged IP.
